findings.issue: The note says Benjamin 'hid in the monasteries of Wadi Habib'. The quoted passage says the opposite: he went to Wadi Habib, found few monks there, then LEFT for Upper Egypt and hid in a small monastery there. The note also generalises two notices into 'places the Miaphysite patriarchs among the old monasteries of Scetis', and 'old' and 'Scetis' are not in the quoted lines (the drafter's own flag says the History does not use 'Scetis' here).

Then Benjamin went forth from the monasteries in Wadi Habib, and departed to Lpper Egypt; and he remained hidden there in a small monastery in the wilderness until the accomplishment of the ten years'. The census's own text for that movement says Reccared brought his bishops 'into the Nicene church of his subjects', and the movement starts c. 560, so it includes the Hispano-Roman Nicene church of Leander and Isidore that existed before 589. The Gothic bishops joined an existing church; they did not found it. Group E reached the same conclusion on this pair and drafted 'argued against' instead (link 67); the merge kept both without reconciling them, and the merge notes do not mention the pair.

findings.issue: Mis-sourced. The only secondary is Macler's footnote dating a coronation. That is not a work giving the consensus reading, so the Widely Accepted bar is not met as drafted. The clause 'the formula of Heraclius's later reign' has no listed source (the drafter's flag admits it rests on census text). But the vendored council of 681 itself shows the see continuing. It calls Sergius 'at one time patriarch of this royal ... city', and his letters to Pope Honorius (pope from 625) place his patriarchate after 622. It then names Pyrrhus, Paul and Peter 'who died bishops of this God-preserved city'. That is continuity of the same see, the same bar links 4, 20 and 22 were held to.
